memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua took all these royal cities and their kings and put them to the sword. He totally destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded. Yet Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds—except Hazor, which Joshua burned - Josh 11:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twice in these verses the writer anchors what Joshua did to an earlier word: "as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded." Joshua is not inventing a campaign of his own; he is carrying out what God had already spoken through Moses years before. There is a long thread of faithfulness running through this story — God speaks, God's servant records it, and a later generation obeys it.

That should encourage us about the Scriptures we hold. God's words do not expire between generations. What He said through Moses still directed Joshua decades later, and what He has spoken in His Word still directs us today. The Bible is not a collection of loose sayings but one connected story of a faithful God keeping His word across the years (Rom 15:4).

Notice too that the cities on their mounds were left standing. God was giving Israel a settled inheritance — homes they did not build, ready to live in (Josh 24:13). Even in a chapter of judgment, God's provision for His people is quietly present. He does not only tear down; He prepares a place. That gentle detail points forward to the greater truth that Jesus has gone to prepare a place for those who are His (John 14:2-3).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How does it strengthen you to see God's word directing generation after generation?
- Where do you need to let Scripture, rather than your own ideas, direct you?
- What has God provided for you that you did not build or earn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that Your word does not fade with time but guides each generation. Let Scripture direct my steps, and thank You for the place Christ prepares. Amen.
